title: KCET 2018 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A

questions.q: 1.0 g of Mg is burnt with 0.28 g of O$_2$ in a closed vessel. Which reactant is left in excess and how much ?
questions.explanation: Moles Mg = 1.0/24 = 0.0417 mol; moles O$_2$ = 0.28/32 = 0.00875 mol. Reaction 2Mg + O$_2$ $\to$ 2MgO needs 0.0175 mol Mg for the O$_2$ available, so Mg is in excess by (0.0417-0.0175)$\times$24 = 0.58 g.

questions.q: The orbital nearest to the nucleus is
questions.explanation: By the (n+l) rule, 4s has (n+l)=4, the lowest among the given orbitals, so it is filled first and lies nearest/lowest in energy.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of radius ?
questions.explanation: H$^-$ has an extra electron so it is the largest, neutral H is smaller, and H$^+$ (a bare proton) is essentially a point charge, the smallest.

questions.q: The intramolecular hydrogen bond is present in
questions.explanation: In o-nitrophenol the -OH and adjacent -NO$_2$ group are close enough to form an intramolecular (chelated) hydrogen bond, unlike the para isomer which forms intermolecular H-bonds.

questions.q: The state of hybrid orbitals of carbon in CO$_2$, CH$_4$ and CO$_3^{2-}$ respectively is
questions.explanation: CO$_2$ is linear (sp), CH$_4$ is tetrahedral (sp$^3$), and CO$_3^{2-}$ is trigonal planar (sp$^2$).

questions.q: For an ideal gas, compressibility factor is
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas, PV = nRT exactly, so Z = PV/nRT = 1 at all conditions.

questions.q: The relationship between K$_p$ and K$_c$ is K$_p$ = K$_c$(RT)$^{\Delta n}$. What would be the value of $\Delta n$ for the reaction NH$_4$Cl (s) $\rightleftharpoons$ NH$_3$ (g) + HCl (g) ?
questions.explanation: $\Delta n$ = moles of gaseous products $-$ moles of gaseous reactants = 2 $-$ 0 = 2.

questions.q: Acidity of BF$_3$ can be explained on which of the following concepts ?
options: Bronsted-Lowry as well as Lewis concept
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ has no OH or H$^+$ to donate; it accepts an electron pair (it is electron deficient), so its acidic behaviour is explained only by the Lewis concept.

questions.q: For the redox reaction x MnO$_4^-$ + y H$_2$C$_2$O$_4$ + z H$^+$ $\to$ m Mn$^{2+}$ + n CO$_2$ + p H$_2$O, the values of x, y, m and n are
questions.explanation: The balanced ionic equation is 2MnO$_4^-$ + 5H$_2$C$_2$O$_4$ + 6H$^+$ $\to$ 2Mn$^{2+}$ + 10CO$_2$ + 8H$_2$O, giving x=2, y=5, m=2, n=10.
In H$_2$O$_2$, oxygen is in the $-1$ state, an intermediate value, so it can be oxidised to O$_2$ (acting as reducing agent) or reduced to H$_2$O/OH$^-$ (acting as oxidising agent).

questions.q: Dead burnt plaster is
questions.explanation: Fully dehydrated (anhydrous) calcium sulphate, formed on strongly heating gypsum, is called dead burnt plaster; it does not set with water.

questions.q: Identify the following compound which exhibits geometrical isomerism :
questions.explanation: But-2-ene (CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_3$) has two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon, allowing cis-trans (geometrical) isomerism; the others do not have a suitable C=C.

questions.q: During the fusion of organic compound with sodium metal, nitrogen present in the organic compound is converted into
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: In Lassaigne's test, carbon, nitrogen (and sulphur, if present) from the organic compound combine with sodium to form sodium cyanide, used to detect nitrogen (Prussian blue test).

questions.q: The reagent 'X' used for the following reaction R-C$\equiv$CR' + H$_2$ $\xrightarrow{X}$ cis-alkene is
questions.explanation: Partially poisoned Pd catalyst (Pd/C, as used in Lindlar-type hydrogenation) adds H$_2$ syn to an alkyne, giving the cis-alkene, whereas Na/liquid NH$_3$ gives the trans-alkene.

questions.q: Which of the following ions will cause hardness in water ?
questions.explanation: Hardness of water is caused by dissolved Ca$^{2+}$ and Mg$^{2+}$ salts, which form insoluble precipitates with soap.

questions.q: Which of the following oxides shows electrical properties like metals ?
questions.explanation: CrO$_2$ shows metallic (in fact ferromagnetic, conducting) behaviour and is used in magnetic recording tapes, unlike the other insulating oxides listed.

questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solutions should have the highest boiling point ?
questions.explanation: Boiling point elevation depends on the total number of particles (van't Hoff factor i). Na$_2$SO$_4$ gives i=3 (2Na$^+$ + SO$_4^{2-}$), higher than the others (i=2), so it has the highest boiling point at equal molarity.

questions.q: The charge required for the reduction of 1 mole of MnO$_4^-$ to MnO$_2$ is
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 in MnO$_4^-$ to +4 in MnO$_2$, a gain of 3 electrons per mole, requiring 3 Faradays of charge.

questions.q: For the reaction, 2SO$_2$ + O$_2$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2SO$_3$, the rate of disappearance of O$_2$ is 2$\times$10$^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. The rate of appearance of SO$_3$ is
questions.explanation: Since 2 mol SO$_3$ forms per 1 mol O$_2$ consumed, rate of SO$_3$ formation = 2 $\times$ (rate of O$_2$ disappearance) = 4$\times$10$^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Which of the following electrolytes will have maximum coagulating value for AgI/Ag$^+$ sol ?
questions.explanation: AgI/Ag$^+$ sol is positively charged, so it is coagulated by anions; by the Hardy-Schulze rule the coagulating power increases sharply with anion charge, and PO$_4^{3-}$ (charge $-3$) is the most effective.

questions.q: Electrolytic refining is used to purify which of the following metals ?
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Copper and zinc are commonly purified by electrolytic refining, where the impure metal is the anode and pure metal deposits at the cathode.

questions.q: Dry ice is
questions.explanation: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, used as a refrigerant since it sublimes directly to gas without leaving residue.

questions.q: Which of the following is an amphoteric oxide ?
questions.explanation: Both V$_2$O$_5$ and Cr$_2$O$_3$ (intermediate oxidation state oxides of transition metals) react with both acids and bases, making them amphoteric.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH$_3$)$_4$Cl(NO$_2$)]Cl is
questions.explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine, chlorido, nitrito-N for N-bonded NO$_2^-$); charge balance with one ionisable Cl$^-$ gives Co oxidation state +3, so the name is tetraamminechloridonitrito-N-cobalt(III) chloride.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true in case of alkyl halides ?
options: They are highly soluble in water
questions.explanation: The C-X bond in alkyl halides is polar due to the electronegativity difference; they cannot hydrogen bond with water, are poorly soluble in water, and being saturated do not undergo addition reactions.

questions.q: Phenol can be distinguished from ethanol by the reagent
questions.explanation: Phenol reacts with bromine water to give a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol instantly, while ethanol does not react this way.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds undergoes haloform reaction ?
questions.explanation: Compounds with a CH$_3$CO- group, like acetone (CH$_3$COCH$_3$), undergo the haloform reaction with a halogen and base to give a haloform.

questions.q: Which of the following will be the most stable diazonium salt (R N$_2^+$ X$^-$) ?
questions.explanation: Aryl diazonium salts (like C$_6$H$_5$N$_2^+$X$^-$) are stabilised by resonance with the aromatic ring, unlike alkyl diazonium salts which decompose readily.

questions.q: Which of the following bases is not present in DNA ?
questions.explanation: DNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine; uracil replaces thymine only in RNA.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a polyamide polymer ?
questions.explanation: Nylon-6,6 is formed by condensation of a diamine and a diacid through amide (-CONH-) linkages, making it a polyamide.

questions.q: In F.C.C. the unit cell is shared equally by how many unit cells ?
questions.note: KEA key credits option 3 ("6"); physically each corner atom of an FCC unit cell is shared among 8 adjacent unit cells, so "8" is the scientifically correct answer.
questions.explanation: In FCC, each corner atom is shared among 8 adjacent unit cells (option "8"), but the official KEA key credits "6".

questions.q: At a particular temperature, the ratio of molar conductance to specific conductance of 0.01 M NaCl solution is
questions.explanation: $\Lambda_m/\kappa$ = 1000/C (with C in mol/L); for C = 0.01 M, this ratio = 1000/0.01 = 10$^5$ cm$^3$ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Isotonic solutions are solutions having the same
questions.explanation: Isotonic solutions are, by definition, solutions that exert the same osmotic pressure at a given temperature.

questions.q: The temperature coefficient of a reaction is 2. When the temperature is increased from 30$^\circ$C to 90$^\circ$C, the rate of reaction is increased by
questions.explanation: A 60$^\circ$C rise equals six 10$^\circ$C intervals; rate increases by (temperature coefficient)$^6$ = 2$^6$ = 64 times.

questions.q: Gold sol is not a
questions.explanation: Gold sol consists of aggregates of gold atoms (a multimolecular, lyophobic, negatively charged colloid), not a single large molecule, so it is not a macromolecular sol.

questions.q: The common impurity present in bauxite is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Bauxite ore commonly contains iron(III) oxide (Fe$_2$O$_3$) as the main impurity, which is removed in Bayer's process.

questions.q: Very pure N$_2$ can be obtained by
options: Treating aqueous solution of NH$_4$Cl and NaNO$_2$
Liquifaction and fractional distillation of liquid air
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition of sodium azide (2NaN$_3 \to$ 2Na + 3N$_2$) gives very pure nitrogen gas, free of other atmospheric gases.

questions.q: Which of the following oxidation states is common for all lanthanides ?
questions.explanation: All lanthanides show a common and most stable +3 oxidation state, though some also show +2 or +4 occasionally.

questions.q: The electronic configuration of transition element "X", is +3, oxidation state is [Ar]3d$^5$. What is its atomic number ?
questions.explanation: Adding back the 3 electrons lost to form the +3 ion ([Ar]3d$^5$) gives the neutral atom configuration [Ar]3d$^6$4s$^2$, i.e. atomic number 18+6+2 = 26 (Fe).

questions.q: n-Propyl chloride reacts with sodium metal in dry ether to give
questions.explanation: This is a Wurtz reaction: 2CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$Cl + 2Na $\to$ CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$-CH$_2$CH$_2$CH$_3$ (n-hexane) + 2NaCl.

questions.q: When the vapours of tertiary butyl alcohol are passed through heated copper at 573 K, the product formed is
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols undergo dehydration (not dehydrogenation) over heated copper, and tert-butyl alcohol gives 2-methylpropene (isobutylene).

questions.q: What is the increasing order of acidic strength among the following ? (i) p-methoxy phenol (ii) p-methyl phenol (iii) p-nitro phenol
questions.explanation: Electron-donating -OCH$_3$ and -CH$_3$ groups decrease acidity (with -OCH$_3$ decreasing it more due to resonance donation), while the electron-withdrawing -NO$_2$ group increases acidity strongly, giving i < ii < iii.

questions.q: Which of the following is more basic than aniline ?
questions.explanation: In benzylamine the -NH$_2$ is on an sp$^3$ carbon, not conjugated with the ring, so its lone pair is fully available, making it more basic than aniline, whose lone pair is delocalised into the ring.

questions.q: The two forms of D-Glucopyranose are called
questions.explanation: The $\alpha$ and $\beta$ forms of D-glucopyranose differ only in configuration at the anomeric carbon (C1), so they are called anomers.

questions.q: Among the following, the branched chain polymer is
questions.explanation: Low density polythene (LDPE) is produced by free-radical polymerisation, which introduces chain branching, unlike the linear HDPE.

questions.q: Edge length of a cube is 300 pm. Its body diagonal would be
questions.explanation: Body diagonal = a$\sqrt3$ = 300 $\times$ 1.732 = 519.6 pm.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a conductor of electricity ?
questions.explanation: In solid NaCl the ions are fixed in the crystal lattice and cannot move, so it does not conduct electricity, unlike molten NaCl or brine where ions are mobile.

questions.q: For a cell reaction involving two electron changes, E$^0_{cell}$ = 0.3 V at 25$^\circ$C. The equilibrium constant of the reaction is
The value of rate constant of a pseudo first order reaction
options: Depends on the concentration of reactants present in small amounts
Depends on the concentration of reactants present in excess
Is independent of the concentration of reactants
questions.explanation: In a pseudo first order reaction, the reactant present in large excess has its concentration folded into the rate constant, so the rate 'constant' depends on the concentration of that excess reactant.

questions.q: (CH$_3$)$_3$SiCl is used during polymerization of organosilicons because
options: The chain length of organosilicon polymers can be controlled by adding (CH$_3$)$_3$SiCl
(CH$_3$)$_3$SiCl improves the quality and yield of the polymer
(CH$_3$)$_3$SiCl does not block the end terminal of silicone polymer
(CH$_3$)$_3$SiCl acts as a catalyst during polymerisation
questions.explanation: (CH$_3$)$_3$SiCl has only one reactive Si-Cl bond, so it caps (end-blocks) growing silicone chains, and controls chain length depending on the amount added.

questions.q: When PbO$_2$ reacts with concentrated HNO$_3$, the gas evolved is
questions.explanation: PbO$_2$ is reduced to Pb$^{2+}$ by concentrated HNO$_3$, and the lattice oxide ion is oxidised, releasing O$_2$ gas: 2PbO$_2$ + 4HNO$_3$ $\to$ 2Pb(NO$_3$)$_2$ + O$_2$ + 2H$_2$O.

questions.q: KMnO$_4$ acts as an oxidising agent in alkaline medium. When alkaline KMnO$_4$ is treated with KI, iodide ion is oxidised to
questions.explanation: In alkaline/neutral medium, KMnO$_4$ oxidises iodide all the way to iodate, IO$_3^-$, being itself reduced to MnO$_2$.

questions.q: [Fe(NO$_2$)$_3$Cl$_3$] and [Fe(O-NO)$_3$Cl$_3$] shows
questions.explanation: The ambidentate NO$_2^-$ ligand can bind through N (nitro) or through O (nitrito), giving linkage isomers.

questions.q: Tertiary alkyl halide is practically inert to substitution by S$_N$2 mechanism because of
questions.explanation: The three bulky alkyl groups around the carbon bearing the halogen block backside attack by the nucleophile, so tertiary halides resist S$_N$2 substitution due to steric hindrance.

questions.q: The products X and Z in the following reaction sequence [benzene + CH$_3$-CH=CH$_2$ $\xrightarrow{AlCl_3/ether, Heat}$ X; X $\xrightarrow{O_2/130^\circ C}$ Y $\xrightarrow{H^+/H_2O, Heat}$ phenol + Z] are
questions.explanation: This is the cumene process: benzene + propene gives cumene (X = isopropylbenzene), which is oxidised to cumene hydroperoxide (Y) and then cleaved by acid to phenol and acetone (Z).

questions.q: The appropriate reagent for the following transformation is [a cyclic hydroxy-ketone converted to the corresponding hydroxy compound with -CH$_2$CH$_3$ in place of -COCH$_3$]
questions.explanation: The carbonyl group is reduced fully to -CH$_2$- while leaving the acid-sensitive -OH group untouched; this selective reduction is achieved by the Wolff-Kishner method (H$_2$N-NH$_2$, KOH/ethylene glycol), unlike the strongly acidic Clemmensen conditions.

questions.q: In the following reaction [toluene $\xrightarrow{CrO_2Cl_2/CS_2}$ X $\xrightarrow{H_3O^+}$ Z] the compound Z is
questions.explanation: This is the Etard reaction: toluene's -CH$_3$ is oxidised by CrO$_2$Cl$_2$ to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde.

questions.q: The reaction of Benzenediazonium chloride with aniline yields yellow dye. The name of the yellow dye is
questions.explanation: Benzenediazonium chloride undergoes coupling with aniline (an azo coupling reaction) at the para position to give the yellow dye p-aminoazobenzene.

questions.q: The glycosidic linkage involved in linking the glucose units in amylose part of starch is
questions.explanation: Amylose is a linear polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose units joined by C$_1$-C$_4$ $\alpha$-glycosidic linkages.

questions.q: Ziegler-Natta catalyst is used to prepare
questions.explanation: Ziegler-Natta catalysts (TiCl$_4$ + Al(C$_2$H$_5$)$_3$) enable controlled, linear polymerisation of ethene at low pressure, giving high density polythene (HDPE).
